html:
The Age of Liberty was the period from 1719 to 1772 when Sweden was governed by its parliament, the Riksdag, rather than by the king.

After the death of Charles XII and defeat in the Great Northern War, Sweden lost its empire. The Estates, nobles, clergy, burghers and peasants, reduced the king to a figurehead. Two parties, the Hats and the Caps, competed for power, sometimes with bribes from foreign states.

In 1766 the Riksdag passed the Freedom of the Press Act, the first law in the world to protect freedom of the press and to give the public access to government documents. King Gustav III ended the era with a coup in 1772. The press law survives as part of the constitution of Sweden. It is often compared with the British parliament of the same time and the Enlightenment.
sum: The Age of Liberty was the period from 1719 to 1772 when Sweden was governed by its parliament, the Riksdag, rather than by the king.
